title: I made it real simple to see where institutions are. Free!
author: KimOnMacro
selftext:
Most traders don't read the COT (Report with current insititutional positions) even though its free.  
  
**Mainly because:**  
**1. It's confusing**   
**2. Didn't find it relevant as its a delayed release**  
**3. They didn't know it exists**

But once you know what to look for, it can be applied in really interesting ways.

Example 1: For Intraday trading, if insitutions bought heavy, theres less fuel left for a fresh breakout.   
So if price suddenly pushes past a level right after a lot of buying already happened, it's more likely to fail and snap back than to keep running. So useful for targetting pullbacks.

Example 2: For Swing Trading, if insitutions added to their positions every week then it's a much stronger trend continuation compared to one big move in a week. So its easier to commit to a long position.  
  
Basically what I've done is visualised it as one of the features in my app.   
  
1. I focussed on making it visually easy (compared to other COT charts online)  
2. I focussed on explaining the data in a way thats easy to apply in a practical trade.

**It's free to use here:**

[https://echelonedgeai.com/](https://echelonedgeai.com/) 

My app is in free beta, but you can still access the COT report on other sites like barchart too

Would love to hear any feedback! Anything you like, don't like, too complicated still etc?

comments.author: krazineurons
comments.body: This is helpful information. What are the data sources?

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Source for the COT is from the CFTC - Free and publicly available!   
Economic releases and prints, values are from financial modeling prep   
Federal reserve bank st louis for broad slower indexes, EIA too for broader opec supplies   
Then multiple news source apis for scraping latest background info + financial juice for breaking newswires etc[](https://www.cftc.gov/)

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: I've also got each source listed on the app under each macro news article too within the app and timestamped.

comments.body:
I am bit confused to read this chart.

[https://imgur.com/ovw8mAN](https://imgur.com/ovw8mAN)

  
Is it just \`big fund\` roughly equal to \`commercial + retail\` ?

  
But this is not an edge right, as the \`big fund\` here are most likely Market Maker, which their job is to sell to you when you buy, and buy from you when you want to sell.

replies.author: tim-r
replies.body: Or did I read it wronly or I choose the time range in a non edge range? ❓

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: I put "Big funds" = non-commercial large speculators (hedge funds, CTAs, asset managers) so separate from the commercials/hedgers category. Not claiming it's "smart money always right," more that positioning getting stretched one way means less room left for the move to extend. So a breakout right after heavy buying is more likely to stall than run! t's a crowding read, not a follow-the-leader signal.

replies.author: KimOnMacro

comments.author: antoniusbethyname
comments.body: Isn’t COT data always one week delayed and released on Fridays?

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: Yep, always a few days behind, CFTC releases Friday for the prior Tuesday's positions. It's not real-time, but positioning doesn't flip day to day so the lag matters less than people assume, it's actually still useful context days later!

comments.author: silphotographer
comments.body: I think it's worth more to have real detailed  studies that proves your hypothesis than the platform itself imho. Market has a nasty tendency to show many human thesis that appear logical and clever don't work.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: You're absolutely right about the logical thesis not really becoming an edge. And honestly, I don't really weight the COT alone as just one indicator etc. My whole app is based on checking things I'd normally check manually (Macro values, news, COT) to stack the probability in my favour but I always match it against technicals and even then won't take a trade if it doesn't seem A+. (Still take losses too, but it's made it very mechanical and repeatable while respecting things outside of TA)

replies.author: silphotographer
replies.body: Without a real sustainable edge you can demonstrate/prove through extensive backtest/stress test, being mechanical and repeatable doesn't mean much. For example, many broker and prop firms would confidently say retails losing money till they implode is very mechanical and repeatable but clearly they aren't  profiting.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: Honestly, no argument there. It's built off my own manual process, not a detailed study so I won't pretend its proven! Appreciate your thoughts though. I'll focus on showing more evidence as I develop it.

replies.author: silphotographer
replies.body:
Well, that depends since your platform is merely to provide the so-called "critical information" more efficiently and ergonomically, you don't necessarily need to prove the edge of your strategy per se. I was just commenting because if I was the target audience, I would want to know  how I can incorporate these information into something that is worth the subscription free or otherwise. 

All I am saying is that if you have some concrete correlation/examples of how your info can be used to genuinely improve trader performance, that's the jackpot.  Business 101 is that your business needs to solve a real socioeconomic needs/wants that people would happily pay for because it brings value to them (real or imagined). Your platform is clear on providing some "critical" information more effectively under one platform but it is not clear what real problem is being solved that people want/need. Most traders  get way more information than they need and they either  get overwhelmed due to abundance paradox. What I imagine most traders want is some clear direction as to how to act more decisively and with confidence (whether they do it with real edge or not is another matter ofc).

To put it simple, imagine you have some black box that absorbs information similar as yours but it spits out simple % probability that it stock will go up or  down or whatever. Most retail traders aka your customers will understand the assignment right a way. If it flashes green 89% then they know what to do. Bunch of information popping out on your platform doesn't help much to most traders.
